text: . President Droupadi Murmu has arrived on a three-day visit to Gujarat today. During her visit, the President will attend key events across Kevadia’s Ekta Nagar and Vadodara. Tomorrow evening, September 22, President Murmu will present the 72nd National Film Awards at Ekta Nagar in Kevadia. Ekta Nagar is all set to host the prestigious awards for the first time, marking a historic shift as the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting takes the nation’s highest film honours beyond the capital to celebrate India’s cinematic diversity under the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’.In a historic move, 72nd National Film Awards ceremony will be held at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat for the first time. Tomorrow, President Droupadi Murmu will preside over the 72nd National Film Awards ceremony at Ekta Nagar honoring outstanding contribution to Indian cinema, including veteran actor Anant Nag with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024. Senior officials, including Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, have reached Ekta Nagar to oversee and witness the historic event. Speaking on the significance of holding the ceremony at Kevadia, Secretary Chanchal Kumar highlighted the inspiring message of the venue.Following the awards ceremony at Kevadia, President Murmu will travel to Vadodara for her final engagements on Wednesday, September 23. She will attend the 75th Annual Convocation of The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda as the Chief Guest to present gold medals to meritorious students. Later in the afternoon, the President will launch Brahma Kumaris’ initiative ‘Spiritual Awakening for World Renewal’ and inaugurate the Global Spiritual Palace at Padra, alongside the virtual national launch of ‘Youth for Viksit Bharat’.

. India and Nepal discussed measures to facilitate greater market access for products of both countries. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry in a statement said that during the two day meeting of Inter-Governmental Sub-Committee (IGSC) on Trade, Transit and Cooperation to Control Unauthorised Trade which concluded yesterday both sides reviewed a wide range of issues. It was related to market access, Customs and trade facilitation, standards, food safety, border infrastructure, rail and road connectivity and other trade-related matters.The Indian delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Department of Commerce, Ujjwal Kumar Ghosh, while the Nepali delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Buddha Bahadur Gurung. The meeting focused on facilitating legitimate trade while strengthening mechanisms to ensure compliance with applicable rules and prevent misuse of preferential trade arrangements. Both sides also reviewed rail and road connectivity, movement of freight, Integrated Check Posts and land-port infrastructure.The discussions focused on improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure and addressing operational bottlenecks affecting bilateral and transit trade. The Ministry said that India and Nepal share close historical, cultural and economic ties and the discussions at the IGSC are expected to further strengthen bilateral trade, transit connectivity and economic cooperation between the two countries.

. In the Asian Games 2026, India’s campaign continues strongly on Day 2 in Japan today. Indian shooters secured 2 Silver medals in Nagoya today. India’s Elavenil Valarivan clinched a silver medal in the women’s 10 metre air rifle event at the Games. The 2025 World Championship bronze medallist Elavenil shot 252.4 points in the final to finish behind Japan’s Hinata Taichi, who won gold with a record 253 points.Earlier, India has secured the silver medal in the women’s 10 metre air rifle team event, with Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod combining to deliver the country’s first medal of the Games. Sonam top-scored for India with 634.1, finishing fourth in the individual qualification, while Olympian Elavenil finished seventh with 633.5 points. China took the gold medal with a total score of 1904.2, while India held on to second spot by scoring 1897.President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated the team on winning the Medal. In a social media post, she said that this commendable achievement has opened India’s medal account at the Games and brings immense pride to the nation.

. India defeated Bangladesh 3-nil, without dropping a single game across three matches, to reach the Men’s Badminton team quarter-finals at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium in Japan today. Lakshya Sen beat Jaman Ayman Ibn, followed by Ayush Shetty’s win over Gourab Singha. Kidambi Srikanth then sealed the tie with a victory over Jumar Al-Amin.Paris 2024 semi-finalist Lakshya comfortably beat Ayman Ibn 21-4, 21-12 to give India a 1-nil lead. Ayush registered a convincing 21-4, 21-13 win over Singha to stretch the lead to 2-nil, before Srikanth sealed the tie with a 21-15, 21-9 victory over Jumar Al-Amin.India will face hosts Japan in the quarter-finals tomorrow, with a win in the tie guaranteeing the team a medal.The Indian women’s team will also face Japan in the quarter-finals tomorrow after beating Kazakhstan 3-nil in its opening tie yesterday.

. Britain has agreed to provide limited support to Saudi Arabia, to counter attacks from Iran-backed Houthis. Riyadh has requested the support after the Houthis, who control the most populous parts of Yemen, intensified their attacks on Saudi ​Arabia, a new front in the wider war that began ​with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February. For the new air-to-air refuelling ​support, Britain will deploy one Voyager plane in ​the coming ⁠days.Britain and Saudi Arabia have been close military allies for decades, with Britain serving as one of the kingdom’s largest arms suppliers. Earlier this year, Britain deployed its Sky Sabre air ​defence system to ​Saudi Arabia to ⁠help protect it from Iranian missile attacks during the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran.British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that this is a time-limited agreement in terms of the assistance that we will provide, but we will keep it under review,” he said, adding ⁠that ​Britain was “playing our part” in the West Asia and also by supporting efforts to keep the Strait of Hormuz open.

. The global ratings agency Moody’s today raised India’s real GDP growth forecast to 7 per cent, ​from its earlier projection of 6 per cent for the current financial year. The agency said that the upward revision reflects the resilience of the Indian economy amid the global shock caused by the conflict in West Asia.The agency expects India to continue growing faster than all other G20 economies. Moody’s said India’s real GDP growth rose to 8.2 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, compared with 7.3 per cent in 2025. The growth was supported by stronger private consumption, robust investment, continued government spending on infrastructure, a revival in private investment and sustained strength in the services sector. However, Moody’s has warned of risks to the outlook.El Niño-related disruptions could push up food prices and affect private consumption. Higher energy and fertiliser import costs, weaker external demand and lower remittances from West Asia could also widen the current account deficit and slow economic growth.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has predicted the formation of a low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal. It is likely to intensify into a deep depression in the next 24 hours, resulting in heavy to very heavy rainfall over coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha today. Heavy rainfall is also likely to prevail over Jharkhand, Karnataka, Konkan, Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gangetic West Bengal, Assam and Meghalaya during the day.Meanwhile, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Andhra Pradesh, Gangetic West Bengal, Konkan, Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal and Telangana are expected to witness thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds during the next two days.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. In Bihar’s Jamui district, police have detained three accused in connection with an incident involving the alleged molestation and indecent behaviour with a minor girl student.Jamui Superintendent of Police Vishwajit Dayal said that an FIR has been registered under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act after a detailed investigation of the viral video. He said that a special investigation team, constituted under the leadership of Sub-Divisional Police Officer Deepti Monali, is conducting raids to arrest the other absconding accused. He added that action is also being taken to remove the uploaded video from social media platforms.Meanwhile, State Women’s Commission Chairperson Apsara has strongly condemned the incident. She said that a team of the Commission will soon meet the victim and gather complete information about the case. She said strict punishment will be ensured for those responsible.Sports Minister and Jamui MLA Shreyasi Singh has also condemned the incident. She said that the administration is taking prompt action in the matter.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Suchika Tariyal on creating history by winning the Bronze Medal in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) at the Asian Games 2026, being held in Nagoya, Japan. In a social media post, the President said that this achievement holds special significance for Indian sport, as it marks the debut of MMA at the Games.President Murmu has also congratulated Himanshu Dhillon on winning the Silver Medal in the Men’s 10m Air Rifle Individual Final and Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil on securing the Bronze Medal in the Men’s 10m Air Rifle Individual event at the Games. She said that their impressive performance reflects focus, dedication and sporting excellence. She wished them continued success and many more accomplishments in the years ahead.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. The Consulate General of India in Dubai organised a Legal Counselling Camp for Indian nationals in Dubai and the Northern Emirates of the UAE, as part of Seva Pakhwada. The camp, held on 21st September, provided pro-bono legal guidance to members of the Indian community on a range of issues, including cybercrime, financial and banking frauds, misuse of Emirates ID and other related legal matters.The counselling camp was conducted on a walk-in basis and did not require any prior appointments. The initiative was aimed at facilitating access to timely legal assistance and providing support to Indian nationals facing legal concerns.

. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar held talks with his counterparts from France, Ecuador, Slovakia and Switzerland on the sidelines of UN General Assembly in New York last night and discussed regional and global issues. Mr Jaishankar arrived in New York City on Sunday, leading the Indian delegation for the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. Mr Jaishankar will address world leaders at the General Debate from the UNGA podium on September 26.His engagements commenced with a meeting with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot. In a social media post Mr Jaishankar said the regular meetings and telecons enable both countries to maintain the momentum of Special Global Strategic Partnership.He said that during the meeting, regional and global issues, specifically the Ukraine and  Gulf crises, were discussed.  Both the leaders also exchanged views on multilateral issues, including the reform of UN Security Council.External Affairs Minister also held a meeting with Ecuador Foreign Minister Roberto Kury, to strengthen economic ties, including energy and pharmaceuticals, mobility, training of personnel, development partnership and cooperation in multilateral fora, including the United Nations.Following his meeting with Slovakia Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar, the External Affairs Minister said that besides discussing the bilateral agenda, they also touched upon ways to deepen our multilateral cooperation.Mr. Jaishankar also held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Hungary Anita Orban. Both the leaders have agreed to work together to deepen ties to advance the bilateral strategic partnership.External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held separate meetings with Switzerland Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis and Nauru President David Adeang, discussing bilateral ties, economic cooperation, and multilateral issues.Sharing details of his meeting on a social media post , Mr Jaishankar said the two sides reviewed the progress in their economic relationship following the entry into force of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement.Earlier, Dr Jaishankar attended the first Visegrád Group (V4) and India Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, involving Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic.

. Google has been fined 403 million euros, or about 463 million US dollars, by Ireland’s Data Protection Commission for breaching European Union privacy rules over the handling of users’ location data. The investigation found that Google had not lawfully or transparently processed location information collected through its Web and App Activity and Location History services.The data privacy regulator also found shortcomings in Google’s processing of personal data through its Location Accuracy feature in the Android operating system. It further said that location data can provide useful services but can also reveal significant and inherently private information about individuals. The fine is the fourth-largest privacy penalty imposed by the Irish watchdog, which has previously issued larger fines against TikTok and Meta.

. India has been ranked first in business climate among forty plus global markets in the latest Business Climate Survey 2026 by the Swedish Chamber of Commerce in India. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal shared this information in a social media post. He said India’s business climate is setting the gold standard for stability, growth and ease of doing business amid global turbulence.The Global Business Climate Survey 2026 edition presents insights from 41 markets, offering a broad view of Swedish companies’ perspectives on doing business abroad. The survey aims to provide a framework for comparing economic performance, outlook, and operating conditions over time in key Swedish export markets. It highlights the challenges companies face and identifies opportunities for Swedish companies considering entry into new markets or expansion in existing ones.

. Marking a new chapter in Indian cinema, President Droupadi Murmu will present the historic 72nd National Film Awards this evening at Ekta Nagar. Instituted in 1954, these awards represent India’s highest cinematic honours, recognising artistic and technical excellence across various categories, namely Feature, Non-Feature, and Writing on Cinema.As part of a major policy initiative by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the awards are being held outside the national capital. The ceremony at Ekta Nagar brings together cinematic talent from across the country, embodying the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’. The president will also honour the veteran actor Anant Nag with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024.The stage is set, and the lights are ready in the iconic Ekta Nagar as Kevadia prepares to host the historic 72nd National Film Awards for the very first time. Renowned actors, acclaimed filmmakers, and technicians from across the country have started arriving at the venue for this grand celebration of Indian cinema.The ceremony honours outstanding cinematic achievements for the year 2024. Among the major feature film announcements, Article 370 was selected for Best Feature Film, with Yami Gautam winning Best Actress for her role in the film. The Best Actor honour is shared by Mammootty for Bramayugam and Kartik Aaryan for Chandu Champion. Rajkumar Periasamy earned Best Direction for Amaran, while Kalki 2898 AD was named Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Randeep Hooda won Best Debut Director for Swatantrya Veer Savarkar. In the non-feature category, the Marathi film Bhangaar was named Best Non-Feature Film, while Director Aanand L Rai was selected for Best Direction for Statue of Unity – Ekta ka Prateek. Ravi Raj Murmu took the Best Debut Director (Non-Feature) honour for the Santhali film, Angen.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will inaugurate the 9th India International Water Week (IIWW) 2026 in New Delhi today. The five day event is being organised on the theme Climate Resilient Water Management. The Jal Shakti Ministry has informed that the international event will witness the participation of the Netherlands and Germany as Partner Countries while fourteen states will participate as partner states and six Central Ministries and Departments have been invited to participate as Partner Ministries and Departments.The Ministry noted that a four day international exhibition will also be organised till 25thof this month. The exhibition will provide a platform for showcasing innovative technologies, products and solutions for sustainable and climate-resilient water management. The Second International WASH Conference 2026 will also be organised by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation. It will focus on drinking water access, sanitation infrastructure, hygiene behaviour and public health, with emphasis on scalable, affordable and sustainable solutions.The Ministry said that deliberations during the event will cover inclusive and equitable water governance, collaboration for optimal use of water resources, technology and community for water security, water in climate-related risk, innovative financing models for water infrastructure and modernisation, sustainable water resources management and water for people and planet.

. Union Minister of New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi has congratulated Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) on its 15th Foundation Day today. In a social media post, Mr Joshi said that SECI has played an important role in advancing India’s renewable energy journey and strengthening the country’s clean energy ecosystem over the past 15 years.

. India’s Women’s Badminton team made a winning start to its Asian Games campaign, with a 3-NIL win over Kazakhstan in the pre-quarterfinal in Aichi, Japan, today. P.V. Sindhu set the tone for India with a dominant 21-7, 21-9 win over Kamila Smagulova in the opening singles rubber. Unnati Hooda then extended India’s advantage with an equally convincing 21-7, 21-10 victory over Alissa Kuleshova. Tanvi Sharma completed the clean sweep with an emphatic 21-5, 21-10 victory over Diana Namenova. India will next face second seeds and hosts Japan in the quarter finals. Japan received a bye in their first-round.

. In Hockey, the Indian Men’s team opened their Asian Games campaign with a 13-1 win over Indonesia today, in their Pool A game in Kakamigahara, Japan. Dilpreet Singh’s four-goal haul led the team towards victory. While  Abhishek, Rajinder Singh, Mandeep Singh, captain Harmanpreet Singh and Jugraj Singh added one apiece. Indonesia’s lone goal came from Aulia Al Ardh in the 33rd minute. The Indian team next faces Sri Lanka on Tuesday.Earlier, Indian Women’s team began their campaign with a dominant 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their Pool B opener at Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium. Deepika Sehrawat was the star of the match scoring eight goals. Ishika Chaudhary scored three, while Lalthantluangi and Neha bagged two each. Indian Women’s team will next take on Indonesia tomorrow.The opening result gave India an early platform in the tournament, with their forwards and penalty-corner attack both making an immediate impact.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. Karam festival, a vibrant celebration of Jharkhand’s rich tribal culture, nature and the bond between brothers and sisters, is being observed across the state today with traditional fervour and enthusiasm. Special cultural and state-level programmes are being organised across Jharkhand to mark the auspicious occasion.Karam festival, one of the most significant celebrations of Jharkhand’s folk culture and nature worship, is being celebrated across the state today with great enthusiasm. Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar attended the program on the eve of Karam festival organised in Bero, Ranchi, as the chief guest and extended greetings to the people of the state. He also delivered a message on nature conservation.Yesterday, a seminar-cum-cultural programme was organised at Audrey House in Ranchi, where the entire premises came alive with Jharkhand’s cultural spirit to the beats of drums, nagadas and mandar, accompanied by traditional Karam songs. A programme was also organised yesterday evening at the Deekshant Mandap in Morabadi, where a tribal fashion show was the main attraction.Karam festival is considered a symbol of crop protection, respect for nature, and the enduring bond between brothers and sisters. On this occasion, sisters observe a Nirjala fast, praying for the well-being and long life of their brothers. This evening, a sacred branch of the Karam tree will be installed at the akhara, followed by community dances and traditional songs throughout the night.In Ranchi, the state capital, as well as in various parts of the state, arrangements have been made for cleanliness, lighting, drinking water and other essential civic facilities at Karam worship sites and akharas. Administrative officials have also reviewed preparations for the Karam festival and have participated in various events.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service. His journey is guided by the principle of “Jan Seva Se Desh Seva” and a continued commitment to public service. Inspired by this vision of service and good governance, the government is working towards the goal of a developed India by 2047. This commitment, through inclusive development and social empowerment, is bringing about a transformation in people’s lives. In this context, the PM-KISAN scheme has added new achievements to the lives of farmers across the country.In Madhya Pradesh, a large number of farmers are benefiting from the PM-KISAN scheme. Under the scheme, eligible farmers receive financial assistance of Rs 6,000 every year in three equal installments, directly into their bank accounts. This support is useful for farmers to meet their needs for fertilisers, seeds and other farming activities. The scheme was started in 2019. So far, more than Rs 4.47 lakh crore have been transferred to farmers through 23 installments. More than nine crore 49 lakh farmers benefited from the 23rd installment.The Central Government has now approved the continuation of the PM-KISAN scheme from 2026-27 to 2030-31. A total financial provision of Rs 3.15 crore has been made for the scheme. Chhindwara farmer Basant Patel said that farmers are happy with the decision to continue the scheme for five more years. Women farmers have also benefited from the scheme. More than Rs 1.6 lakh crore has been given to women farmers so far. The scheme uses digital verification, Aadhaar authentication and Direct Benefit Transfer to send the money directly to farmers.

. The United States is stepping up economic pressure on Iran, warning that Iranian airlines could effectively be shut out of international aviation from tomorrow. Speaking to an American News Channel, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that all Iranian airlines would be “shut down around the world” from September 23 as a result of US economic sanctions. He warned that foreign companies providing services such as fuel, landing facilities or ticket sales to Iranian carriers could also face US sanctions. The move is part of Washington’s broader “Operation Economic Outcast”, aimed at restricting Iran’s access to international financial and commercial networks.At the same time, diplomatic activity around the conflict is likely to be in focus this week in New York, where the 81st UN General Assembly is under way. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is expected to travel to New York on Tuesday as per Iranian state media reports, while Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has already arrived. There are also growing calls for direct Arab-Iranian dialogue.UAE President’s Diplomatic Adviser Dr Anwar Gargash has called for a “new mindset” in relations with Tehran, saying discussions on regional security should take place not only between Iran and the US but also between Iran and Arab states. Qatar, meanwhile, has proposed greater economic interdependence between Iran and its Gulf neighbours as a way of supporting long-term regional stability and a way to guarantee the security of Gulf States. Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari said that Qatar has been working to facilitate an agreement between Iran and the US.In Yemen, Iran-aligned Houthi forces have been pushing to seize strategic highlands in an effort to cut off the Red Sea coast from areas held by the internationally recognised government in Yemen. The developments follow reports that US President Donald Trump had called off planned American strikes on the Houthis at the last minute. Trump has said the US remains in contact with the group and that the Houthis have indicated they will not target US shipping.  The security situation around the Strait of Hormuz has also remained tense.The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency has been monitoring a series of incidents involving commercial vessels in and around the waterway. The latest reported incidents yesterday involved two tankers. One LPG tanker leaving the Strait was struck by debris from unidentified projectiles, while another tanker entering the Strait was reportedly hit by an unknown projectile. Two seafarers sustained minor injuries in one of the incidents. The incidents add to the pressure on commercial shipping through the waterway, where traffic has already fallen sharply amid the wider US-Iran conflict.

. The first V4 + India Foreign Ministers’ Meeting was held on the margins of the Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York yesterday. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar participated in the meeting along with Foreign Ministers of Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic. The meeting was held under the Slovak Presidency of the V4.The Ministers exchanged views on ways to strengthen engagement between India and the Visegrad Group. They acknowledged the strong bilateral relations that exist between India and each of the V4 countries, and noted the potential for the V4+India format to complement and add further momentum to these ties.External Affairs Ministry said that the discussions covered opportunities for cooperation in areas such as trade and investment, technology and innovation, resilient supply chains, defence and security, connectivity, education, mobility and people-to-people exchanges. The Ministers also discussed possibilities for greater interaction between businesses, academic and research institutions and other stakeholders from India and the V4 member states.The Ministers also exchanged perspectives on global and regional developments, peace and security, and cooperation in multilateral fora. Discussions included the need for reformed multilateralism and addressing contemporary global challenges, including those affecting the Global South.The Ministry stated that the inaugural meeting marked an important step in establishing engagement between India and the Visegrad Group at the Foreign Ministers’ level. The V4+India format offers an additional platform for dialogue and cooperation, building upon India’s longstanding and substantive relations with V4 countries.The V4+India group is a diplomatic dialogue format that brings together India and the Visegrád Group (V4)-comprising Central European nations Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic. The Visegrad Group (V4) is a cultural and political alliance that aims to advance cooperation in military, economic, cultural, and energy affairs.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya has congratulated Suchika Tariyal for winning the bronze medal in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) Women’s Traditional-60 kg category at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, Mr Mandaviya said that this is a historic moment as it is India’s first-ever MMA medal at the Asian Games. Dr Mandaviya has also congratulated Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil, Parth Rakesh Mane and Himanshu Dhillon on securing the Silver Medal in the Men’s 10m Air Rifle Team event at the Asian Games 2026.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. The Uttar Pradesh government has carried out a major administrative reshuffle, transferring 34 IAS officers last night. District Magistrates of 14 districts have also been changed. According to the transfer order, several senior officers have been assigned new responsibilities, along with changes in the district administration. The districts where new District Magistrates have been appointed include Hardoi, Moradabad, Etah, Amethi, Kushinagar, Kanpur Nagar, Sant Kabir Nagar, Pilibhit, Ballia, Baghpat, Mahoba, Bijnor, Hathras and Hamirpur.The reshuffle is among the significant changes in the state bureaucracy, with new postings given to senior IAS officers as well as district-level officials.

. The Indian men’s chess team secured an emphatic 3-1 victory over Holland, while the Indian women’s team suffered a shocking defeat to Poland in the fifth round of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The Indian men extended their perfect run to five consecutive match wins, placing them at the top of the leaderboards alongside Uzbekistan and Germany.R Praggnanandhaa bounced back from a string of draws to score a brilliant victory over an in-form Anish Giri. Arjun Erigaisi fought hard to secure a draw against Jorden Van Foreest. Nihal Sarin comfortably held a draw against veteran Loek Van Wely. D Gukesh continued his sublime form by defeating Erwin l’Ami, picking up his fourth individual win in five games.Indian women’s team faced their first major speed bump of the tournament. A critical loss by R Vaishali proved costly, as the rest of the squad couldn’t make up the deficit, resulting in a narrow 1.5-2.5 defeat. This loss dropped the women’s team to eighth place, though six rounds still remain to mount a comeback.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. The Reserve Bank of India has extended an existing KYC facility available to Non-Resident Indians and Persons of Indian Origin to Foreign Portfolio Investors, allowing banks to accept original certified copies of KYC documents certified by specified authorities abroad.Under the amended directions, banks may accept an original certified copy of Aadhaar-related proof or an officially valid document for FPIs, with the certification done by specified authorities. The certified copies may be attested by authorised officials of overseas branches of Scheduled Commercial Banks registered in India, branches of overseas banks having relationships with Indian banks, Notary Public abroad, Court Magistrate, Judge, or the Indian Embassy/Consulate General in the country where the non-resident customer resides.The amendment was issued on Friday through the RBI (Commercial Banks – Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026 and came into effect immediately.

. India has joined other G20 nations in adopting four consensus outcomes covering household energy access, infrastructure approvals, water reuse and secure critical-mineral supply chains. At a three-day meeting in Houston, Texas, hosted by the White House National Energy Dominance Council, the departments of Energy and the Interior, and the Environmental Protection Agency.For homes, they backed scalable options like using liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to quickly replace traditional biomass, which helps developing countries switch to cleaner cooking fuels. They also called for faster and more predictable government permitting processes for energy infrastructure projects.Additionally, the nations launched a voluntary water-reuse initiative to recycle water based on its quality across farming, manufacturing, and community sectors. Finally, the members agreed to work together voluntarily to secure and diversify the supply chains of critical minerals through shared data, innovation, and joint investments.

. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. World Rhino Day is being observed today across the world, including India, to raise awareness about protecting the five remaining rhinoceros species.This year’s theme, “Keep the Five Alive,” calls for stronger efforts to protect rhino habitats, prevent poaching and curb the illegal trade in rhino horn. Only around 27-thousand rhinos remain in the wild, compared with nearly five lakh a century ago.India is home to the greater one-horned rhinoceros, whose population has recovered to nearly four thousand in India and Nepal, from around 200, following sustained conservation efforts.A programme is being organised today at Neelpara Ground in Alipurduar to mark this day.

. India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement will come into force from 20th of October this year. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that the Agreement provides duty-free access for 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand. He said, the strategic partnerships reflects the shared ambition to deepen this cooperation and aspirational goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to almost 35 thousand crore rupees in the next 4 to 5 years.This will open new opportunities for Indian exports including textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and processed food products. At the same time, New Zealand will gain enhanced and access to the Indian market for products including wood, wool, sheep meat, and raw leather hides. The Agreement also creates new opportunities in services, investment and professional, student and youth mobility, including enhanced pathways for Indian professionals and students.It provides for facilitating 20 billion US dollars of investment into India and strengthens bilateral cooperation in areas including agricultural productivity, pharmaceuticals and medical devices, traditional medicine and AYUSH, technology and trade facilitation. India and New Zealand share longstanding and close relations, anchored in strong people-to-people ties and expanding cooperation across trade and investment, agriculture, education, sports, technology and other areas. The FTA represents a significant step in further strengthening these ties and creating new opportunities for businesses and communities in both countries.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah will inaugurate the Third National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States and Union Territories in New Delhi today. The Ministry of Home Affairs has informed that during the event Mr Shah will also lay the foundation stones for the new complexes of Narcotics Control Bureau Zones in Lucknow and Dehradun.The two-day conference, based on the theme ‘United Resolve, Shared Responsibility ‘, will focus on the progress of targets assigned to the ANTF and initiatives undertaken in combating the menace of drug trafficking and substance abuse across the country. During the event, Mr Shah will also release Television Commercials to spread awareness against drug abuse.The Ministry of Home Affairs said that the heads of Anti-Narcotics Task Forces from 36 states and Union Territories will participate in this conference. This discussion will help the participating states, departments, and agencies to move forward with a renewed commitment towards effectively combating drug trafficking across the country over the next three years.The national event will also seek to further deepen a future-ready partnership between Narcotics Control Bureau and Anti-Narcotics Task Force to combat drug abuse and realise the vision of a Drug-Free India.

. The National Steering Committee (NSC) has approved 320 Crore rupees for Kurukshetra ITI cluster in Haryana under the PM SETU scheme. Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme is the government’s flagship initiative to raise the standard of vocational training by inculcating modern infrastructure, industry-led curricula, and strong industry partnerships.The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship informed that with this approval, the total approved amount under PM SETU has increased to 2491 crore rupees across 10 ITIs clusters. The ministry noted that the increment highlighted the government’s commitment to transform Industrial Training Institutes into future-ready and industry-led centres of excellence.Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary said that bringing industry closer to ITIs will create stronger employment pathways for our youth. He also added that, with strong industry partnerships, the government is working to ensure that young people are equipped with the skills, exposure and opportunities required to participate meaningfully in India’s growth story.

. In the Asian Games, India secured a double podium finish in the men’s 10-metre air rifle event in Nagoya, Japan. Himanshu Dhillon won the silver medal with a score of 252.4, while Rudrankksh Patil clinched the bronze with 230.9. Earlier, India had also won the silver medal in the men’s 10-metre air rifle team event.The Indian trio of Himanshu Dhillon, Parth Mane and Rudrankksh Patil finished second with a total score of 1890.1, behind China’s score of 1899.0. In Mixed Martial Arts, Suchika Tariyal bagged the bronze medal after losing 0-2 to Singapore’s Hui Hoon Toe in the women’s 60-kilogram traditional semi-final.Earlier, Elavenil Valarivan, Vidarsa Vinod and Sonam Maskar won silver in the women’s 10-metre air rifle team event, while Elavenil also claimed silver in the Women’s 10m Air Rifle Individual event, finishing just behind Japan’s Hinata Taichi.

. Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel today said that India’s journey in Pharmacovigilance has been a remarkable example of self-reliance over the years. She said this while releasing the 7th Edition of the National Formulary of India in New Delhi. The Minister said that currently more than one thousand one hundred Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring Centres are operational in the country and the Government aims to increase this number up to the primary health facility level.She also said that 25 countries in the world recognise and accept the Indian pharmacopoeia and added that the country now provides pharmacovigilance data to the WHO patient safety database. The Minister highlighted that India has risen from the 123rd rank in 2014 to the 8th rank in providing this data to WHO. India achieved this milestone in the year 2025. On the occasion, the Minister appealed to the citizens to avoid any form of self-medication, follow professional prescriptions, and never ignore a sudden or unexpected side effect of any medicinal drug.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil, Parth Rakesh Mane and Himanshu Dhillon on winning the Silver Medal in the Men’s 10m Air Rifle Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, she said that their precision and outstanding performance have brought great pride to the nation. President Murmu extended best wishes to them for many more laurels ahead.

. Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava has said that India’s digital foundation, built through Aadhaar and strengthened by the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and ABHA IDs, has enabled the country to build a scalable and interoperable digital health ecosystem. Speaking at a fireside chat on ‘Grounding the Frontier: A Global South AI Framework’ in New York, she highlighted India’s experience in using AI and digital health innovations for the Global South.She said AI models must learn from contextual and representative data to deliver solutions that are relevant to the populations they serve. She also highlighted the use of AI in clinical decision support, longitudinal health records and identifying disease hotspots. Ms Srivastava highlighted the Strategy for AI in Healthcare (SAHI) as a framework for responsible and effective adoption of AI in health, underlining India’s experience in taking technology-enabled solutions to scale. The discussion also explored how AI can help advance healthcare and development outcomes across the Global South and contribute to progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals.

. The Enforcement Directorate (ED), Delhi Zonal Office, has provisionally attached equity shares of a company having a current market value of more than Rs 42 Crore, in connection with an alleged large-scale financial fraud involving a collective investment scheme.ED initiated the investigation based on an FIR registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation. Subsequently, CBI filed a charge-sheet and a supplementary charge-sheet against 33 accused persons for their role in running the illegal investment scheme.According to the charge-sheets, the accused entities and persons were fraudulently mobilising over Rs 48,000 crore from lakhs of investors across India under the pretext of sale and development of agricultural land. Investors were induced to invest and made to sign misleading documents, such as agreements, powers of attorney, and other instruments. In most cases, land was never delivered, and approximately Rs 48,000 crore remains unpaid to investors.ED has attached over 29.46 lakh equity shares of the company, purchased for more than Rs 30 Crore. The agency alleged that the funds used for the purchases were diverted from money mobilised from gullible investors. Further investigation is in progress.

. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has cautioned that the semiconductor industry should be prepared for cyberattacks and any kind of disruption by countries that do not want India to move up the semiconductor value chain.Talking to a media house in New Delhi, Mr Vaishnaw said India has to continuously be watchful of the potential geopolitical risks that will arise because it is now emerging as a country that can design and manufacture chips. He added that this will be seen as a threat by many other established players. Mr Vaishnaw said it is an industry which requires lots of effort on every front. He added that the industry, the government, and the state governments have to work in tandem.

. Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan held telephonic parleys with his counterparts in Kuwait, Egypt and Türkiye to discuss regional developments and diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions amid Saudi-Houthi hostilities.Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed that Saudi forces carried out 28 airstrikes on Yemen’s Taiz, Al-Jawf and Marib provinces in the past 24 hours, taking the alleged total to 760. The Houthis also claimed missile and drone attacks on targets in Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu.Meanwhile, the US Mission in Saudi Arabia restricted official and personal travel by US government employees to Taif and Yanbu, citing the security situation following Houthi attacks.

. India won three medals in shooting at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, today.In the men’s 10-meter air rifle individual event, Himanshu Dhillon won the silver medal, while Rudrankksh Patil secured the bronze. India also bagged a silver medal in the men’s team event of the same competition.Yesterday, Elavenil Valarivan won the silver medal in the women’s individual 10-metre air rifle event. India also bagged a silver medal in the women’s team event of the same competition. With this, India has won a total of five medals in Shooting so far, including four silver and one bronze.Suchika Tariyal has become the first athlete from the country to win a medal in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA). Suchika secured the bronze medal in the 60 kg category.In the medal tally, India is currently in 12th place with a total of six medals, including four silver and two bronze.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil, Himanshu Dhillon, and Parth Rakesh Mane on winning the silver medal in the Men’s 10 meter Air Rifle Team event at the Asian Games. In a social media post, Mr. Modi commended the trio, stating that their focus, consistency, and exceptional teamwork have made the entire nation proud.In addition to the team success, the Prime Minister lauded the athletes for their individual achievements in the Men’s 10 meter Air Rifle event. Congratulating Himanshu Dhillon on winning the silver medal, Mr Modi praised his composure and remarkable accuracy under pressure, noting that his performance was a source of national pride.Extending his congratulations to Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil for securing the bronze medal, Mr Modi appreciated his focus and discipline throughout the competition, wishing him continued success in all his future endeavors.
